hints.title: Unifying Home and Away Match Perspectives
hints.text: Unify match records from both the home team and away team perspectives using union all.

hints.title: Calculating Match Points and Goal Stats
hints.text: Assign 3 points for a win, 1 point for a tie, and 0 points for a loss. Track goals scored and goals conceded.

hints.title: Aggregating and Sorting League Table
hints.text: Join with the teams table to include teams with played matches, computing matches played, points, and goal differences.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH AllMatches AS (
    SELECT home_team_id AS team_id, home_team_goals AS goals_for, away_team_goals AS goals_against,
           CASE WHEN home_team_goals > away_team_goals THEN 3 WHEN home_team_goals = away_team_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS points
    FROM Matches
    UNION ALL
    SELECT away_team_id AS team_id, away_team_goals AS goals_for, home_team_goals AS goals_against,
           CASE WHEN away_team_goals > home_team_goals THEN 3 WHEN away_team_goals = home_team_goals THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS points
    FROM Matches
)
SELECT
    t.team_name,
    COUNT(*) AS matches_played,
    SUM(m.points) AS points,
    SUM(m.goals_for) AS goal_for,
    SUM(m.goals_against) AS goal_against,
    SUM(m.goals_for) - SUM(m.goals_against) AS goal_diff
FROM Teams t
JOIN AllMatches m ON t.team_id = m.team_id
GROUP BY t.team_id, t.team_name
ORDER BY points DESC, goal_diff DESC, t.team_name ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(M + T log T) where M is matches and T is teams
complexity.notes: Unpivot of fixture results followed by team aggregation and composite ranking.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Separate queries for home and away records require complex full outer join merging.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: UNION ALL streaming doubles match rows without sorting overhead.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should unpivot matches symmetrically and order by points, goal difference, and team name.

import pandas as pd

def league_statistics(teams: pd.DataFrame, matches: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    home = matches[["home_team_id", "home_team_goals", "away_team_goals"]].copy()
    home.columns = ["team_id", "goals_for", "goals_against"]
    home["points"] = home.apply(lambda r: 3 if r["goals_for"] > r["goals_against"] else (1 if r["goals_for"] == r["goals_against"] else 0), axis=1)
    
    away = matches[["away_team_id", "away_team_goals", "home_team_goals"]].copy()
    away.columns = ["team_id", "goals_for", "goals_against"]
    away["points"] = away.apply(lambda r: 3 if r["goals_for"] > r["goals_against"] else (1 if r["goals_for"] == r["goals_against"] else 0), axis=1)
    
    all_m = pd.concat([home, away])
    agg = all_m.groupby("team_id").agg(
        matches_played=("points", "count"),
        points=("points", "sum"),
        goal_for=("goals_for", "sum"),
        goal_against=("goals_against", "sum")
    ).reset_index()
    agg["goal_diff"] = agg["goal_for"] - agg["goal_against"]
    
    res = teams.merge(agg, on="team_id")
    res = res.sort_values(by=["points", "goal_diff", "team_name"], ascending=[False, False, True])
    return res[["team_name", "matches_played", "points", "goal_for", "goal_against", "goal_diff"]]
solutions.approach: Concat unpivot and groupby aggregation in pandas
